scope: Historical CPU latency priors; no final20 rows used for fitting.
concurrency: Two pipelines maximum; provider-family serialization recorded in the source protocol.

fields.call_elapsed: Elapsed HTTP request-to-complete-response seconds, including provider/network/queueing.
fields.pipeline_seconds: Docker pipeline wall duration, including startup, preparation, tools and calls.

fit.slope: Nonnegative weighted median of (elapsed-intercept)/weighted_cost, using weighted_cost as the sample weight.
fit.selection: Choose the intercept/slope pair minimizing in-sample unweighted request MAE.
fit.tail: Empirical quantiles of actual/predicted latency on the same historical data; not calibrated coverage.
fit.rounding: Rounded module prior = fixed_request_seconds, seconds_per_weighted_token, upper_multiplier. Small-plain intercept uses a conservative0.5s floor.

task_overhead_scope: Observed inter-request gaps include planning/SDK/disk and tool work; these are not pure tool-time measurements. Same-task search has only2 gaps.
non_api_pipeline_seconds: Typical203–238s across100-task historical pipelines; one classic run288s. Startup cannot be separated from these totals.
limitations: Prior fit and tail estimates are descriptive in-sample statistics, not SLA guarantees.
Effective output throughput includes all HTTP latency and is reported only for calls with at least32 output tokens; it is not GPU decode throughput.
Weighted-token slope confounds input/output mix, queueing, prompt length and policy.
Older non-serialized train/cal/test data had429 errors and were not used for the inline priors.
Public100 was previously evaluated for other objectives and is now development data for latency; the new SLA panel must remain fresh.
Service drift, reasoning caps, CPU contention and concurrent requests can invalidate historical speed estimates.
